concept.name: Basis point
concept.definition: A unit of measure for interest rates and yields equal to one one-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%). It is the standard unit for quoting yield changes, spreads, and rate moves.
concept.intuition: It is the 'cent' of interest rates: saying 'up 25 basis points' unambiguously means up 0.25 percentage points.
concept.mechanics: Yields, spreads, and rate changes are multiplied by 100 to convert percentage points to basis points; e.g. the Federal Reserve describes changes in the federal funds target in basis points, and DV01 measures value change per one basis point.
concept.formula: 1 bp = 0.01% = 0.0001 in decimal; value in bp = value in percent × 100.
concept.failure_modes: Confusion between basis points and percent (or between relative percent change and percentage-point change) causes order-of-magnitude errors in P&L and risk calculations.
concept.misconceptions: A '1% rise in rates' is ambiguous; professional usage distinguishes a 100 bp (one percentage point) rise from a 1 percent relative increase, which are very different.
concept.example: If the 10-year Treasury yield moves from 4.25% to 4.50%, it has risen 25 basis points.
